issues.description: The problem statement and plotting helper refer to a function named simulate_msd_one_round(n_shots: int, p: float), but the template repository defines simulate_one_round(...) (note the different name). This name mismatch means students following the template will either implement the wrong function or encounter NameError when plot_msd calls simulate_msd_one_round. The solution implements simulate_msd_one_round, which demonstrates the intended name, so the template's function name is inconsistent with both the problem text and the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the function name consistent across all artifacts. Rename the template's simulate_one_round to simulate_msd_one_round (keeping the same signature), or update the problem statement and plot_msd calls to use simulate_one_round. Prefer renaming the template function to simulate_msd_one_round to match the specification and the solution.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution refer to the function simulate_msd_one_round(...) but the template file defines a function named simulate_one_round(...). This mismatch means students implementing the function named in the problem will not find the corresponding stub in the starter code (or tests expecting simulate_msd_one_round may not call the template function), creating confusion about where to implement the required behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template stub simulate_one_round(...) in msd.py to simulate_msd_one_round(...) so its name matches the function specified in the problem statement and the solution (or alternatively update the problem/tests to expect simulate_one_round). Ensure signature and docstring match the expected simulate_msd_one_round API.
